questions: Does the platform reproduce 14 of 20 oval completions with your final controller?
On the held-back or final track, does any run reach progress above 0.5 on the s-bend or slalom?

intent: Final-iteration platform: keep the iteration 7 and 10 geometry exactly (seven 16 mm sensors at y = 0.02 m, x = ±0.06 m at 0.02 m pitch, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body, 0.6 kg). This is the only configuration with oval completions (14 of 20, score 303.8). No geometry change is made, so the final unseen-track race uses a platform with known behaviour. Expected: oval-type completions near 70 percent on a similar track, and the controller carries the rest.
learning: Across 11 iterations, the only geometry changes that helped were the 16 mm footprint, the seven-sensor ±0.06 m span at y = 0.02 m, and light inertia (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body). Track width, wheel radius, the ±0.07 m span and the 12 mm footprint each reduced or removed completions. max_error stayed at about 0.061 to 0.064 m through every geometry change, so the off-track floor is not a geometry lever.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design raced here is the one the final unseen-track evaluation will use. No further geometry test can be run, so the choice should be the platform with the best evidence. Iteration 7 and its identical re-run in iteration 10 scored 303.8, the best result so far, with 14 of 20 oval completions. Iteration 8 (12 mm) dropped oval completions to 0, and iteration 9 (±0.07 m span, unscaled weights) also dropped them to 0, so both of those changes are rejected. Iteration 6 showed that a larger wheel radius cut oval progress, and iteration 4 showed that the heavier 0.8 kg robot lost progress. The Integrator's own feedback keeps the ±0.06 m, 16 mm, y = 0.02 m platform. The s-bend and slalom have never finished, and no geometry tested has moved max_error off the 0.06 m floor. Any untested change (for example wheel_track 0.11 m) risks losing the oval completions that carry most of the score, and it cannot be verified before the final race. I therefore keep the proven platform unchanged. The gains and weight scale are the Integrator's responsibility.
